what: A scene panel stuck to the screen is erased by a soft wavy-edge mask tied to scroll — the position of a mask image 5×2 times larger than the panel (left opaque, wavy boundary, right transparent) moves from 0% 0% → 130% 70%, so the wave boundary sweeps the panel toward the lower right and the panel below is revealed (scrub 1, no curve). The measuring range can be set by an empty block behind the panel (one screen), and once fully erased the panel steps out of the way of clicks. look: wave-r is an inverted wave, a panel pushed in from the right (-30% 0% → 100% 30%), fog is a fog mass (300% 450%), vert is a wave descending vertically (500% 300%).

options.look: Mask shape types — wave (default, horizontal wave 500% 200%) · wave-r (inverted wave) · fog (fog 300% 450%) · vert (vertical wave 500% 300%)
options.to: Mask slot end point ”x y” (%, default 130 70)
options.on: Measure position — self (default, the panel itself) · next (the panel’s next sibling — the gap after the panel) · parent
options.size: When resizing the mask image, use values like “500% 200%”

use: …Hero…

from.where: index.html .ky-maskarea__el (Hero is wiped away by a wave — original updateMaskEffect: mask-hrzn 500% 200%, 0% 0% → 130% 70%, blank 20% bottom → bottom bottom, scrub 1)
index.html .ky-stage__el (the Know plate pushes in as an upside-down wave — original mask-hrzn-r -30% 0% → 100% 30%, blank after the photo set top bottom → bottom bottom)
index.html .ky-about (the ‹Knowing› panel slides out in a wave — original 0% 0% → 130% 0%)

note: The original masking image (webp) was not carried over — it was redrawn as a blurred SVG with the same structure (opaque left · wavy edge · transparent right) — the wave curves differ from the original. The original switches to opacity on phones, which is split by matchMedia in the consuming code
